decisions.quote: Experiment 2 revealed that the word class effect could not be separated from the imageability effect: Naming latencies were sensitive to distractor imageability (see Lupker, 1979 ), but were not sensitive to distractor word class when imageability was controlled. These results conflict with the results of Pechmann and colleagues (2004 ; Pechmann & Zerbst, 2002 ).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. While Experiment 1 directly replicates Pechmann and Zerbst (2002, Experiment 4; DOI 10.1037/0278-7393.28.1.233, represented by shipped row 899) in German, Pechmann, Garrett, and Zerbst (2004, DOI 10.1037/0278-7393.30.3.723) is a separate published study that tested the picture-word interference grammatical class effect in English (Experiments 2 and 3) to rule out German grammatical gender confounds. In Experiment 2 of the present paper, the authors test native English speakers in sentence-frame and bare-noun picture naming while orthogonally manipulating distractor word class and imageability to retest whether the word class effect reported by Pechmann et al. (2004) and Pechmann and Zerbst (2002) holds when imageability is controlled, and explicitly conclude in the General Discussion that Experiment 2 conflicts with Pechmann et al. (2004; Pechmann & Zerbst, 2002). Because Pechmann, Garrett, and Zerbst (2004) is a distinct empirical article whose English PWI word-class finding is empirically retested and contrasted in Experiment 2 and is absent from shipped row 899, target_index 1 is a genuinely missing original target.
